bullets: Two-light setups solve 80% of commercial problems — once internalized, this heuristic makes the rest of the lighting decisions easier, and its second-order effects are the part most people miss.
On location, the first decision is always whether to shape the existing light rather than replace it; this framing determines which trade-offs the shoot will involve.
Frame and light are inseparable — lighting design choices cannot be evaluated independently of composition, a pattern observed at teams using Peak Design.
Color temperature mistakes cost more shoots than focus mistakes; ignoring this leads to rebuilding the approach from scratch a year later.
Outside of Profoto-class tooling, the failure mode is harder to spot — lesser equipment hides problems rather than surfacing them.
Adopting Adobe or Capture One in the workflow makes lighting trade-offs visible, turning implicit decisions into explicit ones.
Trade-offs around frame cross-cut every other lighting design decision, from strobe lighting to shaping existing light.
Running one idea for two weeks beats trying everything at once — improvement comes from iteration rather than wholesale change.
